lesson_title: The Note That Never Changed: the Doppler Effect
hook_text: The siren never changed its note. Your ears got played — and the same trick proves the universe is expanding.
clip_script: A fire engine screams past you and the note sags — high wail coming in, deep groan going out. Here's the twist: ride inside the cab, and the siren holds ONE steady note the entire trip. The siren tells the crew the truth all day. It lies only to you. Why? Sound is a parade of pressure crests. Engine driving at you: every crest launches from a little closer than the last, so they hit your ear bunched up — more crests per second, higher pitch. Engine past you: every crest launches from farther away — stretched spacing, fewer per second, the note sinks. Nothing about the siren changed. Motion re-spaced the waves. Now aim that trick at the sky. Light is a wave too, and every element stamps a fingerprint of lines into its light. Astronomers find hydrogen's fingerprint in galaxy after galaxy — intact, but slid toward the red. Slid red means racing away. And the farther the galaxy, the bigger the slide. Almost everything in the sky is leaving, and the farthest things are leaving fastest. One sagging siren on your street corner — and it's the same physics that proves the universe is expanding.
visual_style: Split screen of a pedestrian wincing at a passing fire engine versus a calm crew inside the cab with a flat steady waveform; wave crests drawn bunching and stretching across the road; then a zoom out from the street to a star field where barcode fingerprints slide toward red, farther ones sliding more.
mood: Mischievous street-level reveal opening out into cosmic awe.
pacing: Fast siren gag up front, beat of quiet on the steady in-cab note, then an accelerating pull-back to the expanding sky.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and catch the whole universe in the act of leaving.
